title: Invariant rank decomposition and gluing of monic equations
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with maps $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$, and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] satisfying the groupoid laws [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$, and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. There exists a finite set $I\subset\mathbf Z_{\ge1}$ and a disjoint open-and-closed decomposition $U=\coprod_{r\in I}U_r$ into nonempty affine opens for which $R_r=s^{-1}(U_r)=t^{-1}(U_r)$ is affine, the structure maps restrict to a groupoid $(U_r,R_r)$, and both $s_r,t_r:R_r\to U_r$ have degree $r$. Put $A_r=\Gamma(U_r,\mathcal O)$, $B_r=\Gamma(R_r,\mathcal O)$, $\sigma_r=s_r^\sharp$, $\tau_r=t_r^\sharp$, and $C_r=\{b\in A_r:\sigma_r(b)=\tau_r(b)\}$. Restriction gives ring isomorphisms
$$
\rho_A:A\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{r\in I}A_r,\qquad
\rho_B:B\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{r\in I}B_r,\qquad
\rho_C:C\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{r\in I}C_r.
$$
They satisfy $\rho_B(\sigma(a))_r=\sigma_r(\rho_A(a)_r)$ and $\rho_B(\tau(a))_r=\tau_r(\rho_A(a)_r)$, and $\rho_C$ is the restriction of $\rho_A$. For every $a\in A$, put $a_r=\rho_A(a)_r$. If $I\ne\emptyset$ and polynomials [def-weil-polynomial-ring] $P_r(T)=T^r+\sum_{j<r}p_{r,j}T^j\in C_r[T]$ satisfy $P_r(a_r)=0$ in $A_r$ for every $r\in I$, let $d=\max I$ and write
$$
T^{d-r}P_r(T)=T^d+\sum_{j<d}q_{r,j}T^j,\qquad
q_j=\rho_C^{-1}((q_{r,j})_{r\in I}),\qquad
Q(T)=T^d+\sum_{j<d}q_jT^j\in C[T].
$$
Then $Q$ is monic, its coefficientwise restriction to $C_r[T]$ is $T^{d-r}P_r$, and $\rho_A(Q(a))_r=a_r^{d-r}P_r(a_r)=0$ for every $r$, so $Q(a)=0$. If $U=\emptyset$, then $I=\emptyset$, $A$ is the zero ring, and $T\in C[T]$ is a monic annihilator of its unique element. The existence of the family $P_r$ on nonempty pieces is not asserted.

proof.text: Convert Scheme.IsGroupoid to IsGroupoidScheme by the pullback universal property, and apply lem-a1-affine-groupoid-invariant-rank-strata. Choose its restricted maps, and convert their laws back using pullback uniqueness. This gives the stated rank pieces, all restricted maps and all compatibility equations.

proof.text: For any pairwise disjoint open cover of a scheme X, the ring homomorphism from global sections to the product of sections on its opens is injective by sheaf separatedness. A tuple is compatible: restrictions coincide on a repeated open, and different opens have empty intersection. Unique sheaf gluing makes the map surjective, also for an empty index type. Transfer along Opens.topIso to global sections of the open subschemes. Apply to U and to its inverse images V under s; compose with GammaSpecIso to obtain rhoA and rhoB. GammaSpecIso naturality and the restricted source/target squares give the component formulas.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), first paragraph: reduction and recombination over the invariant rank pieces of Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free); product of section rings as in Tag 01I5 (schemes-lemma-disjoint-union-affines).

proof.text: Define C and C_r to be the specified equalizer subrings. Define the ring homomorphism C to the product of C_r by restricting rhoA. The component formulas show it is well-defined. Injectivity follows from rhoA; for a tuple b in the product equalizer, the element rhoA inverse of its underlying tuple is invariant by injectivity of rhoB. Thus this homomorphism is bijective and gives rhoC, with the asserted underlying-element formula.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), first paragraph: reduction and recombination over the invariant rank pieces of Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free); product of section rings as in Tag 01I5 (schemes-lemma-disjoint-union-affines).

proof.text: Let d be the finite supremum of I, q_r = X^(d-r) P_r, b_j = rhoC inverse of the tuple of coefficients of q_r, and Q = X^d plus sum over j<d of C(b_j) X^j. Positive degree r makes P_r nonzero; its monicity and degree give q_r monic of natural degree d. Mathlib degree_sum_fin_lt and monic_X_pow_add prove Q monic. Applying the r-th coefficient ring homomorphism to Q and using rhoC applied to its inverse gives the monic expansion q_r.as_sum, hence Q restricts to q_r.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), first paragraph: reduction and recombination over the invariant rank pieces of Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free); product of section rings as in Tag 01I5 (schemes-lemma-disjoint-union-affines).

proof.text: The underlying-element formula for rhoC identifies the two coefficient ring homomorphisms into A_r. The hom_eval2 and eval2_map identities therefore identify the r-th component of Q(a) with the evaluation of q_r at a_r, namely a_r^(d-r) P_r(a_r). The supplied root equation makes this zero. Injectivity of rhoA gives Q(a)=0.

proof.text: For empty Spec A, the rank-strata theorem gives I empty and PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton gives Subsingleton A. Polynomial.X is monic over every ring, including the zero ring, and its evaluation in A is zero by subsingleton elimination. The section product construction above already covers empty index types.
